claims.statement: Current MDCG guidance states that manufacturers must operate a structured, proactive PMS system within the quality system, gather and record data continuously throughout device life, and use results to update technical documentation and corrective or preventive action.

The MDCG PSUR guidance says a PSUR summarizes systematically gathered post-market data, benefit-risk conclusions, and relevant preventive or corrective actions for competent authorities and notified bodies.
Four EUDAMED modules, including actor and UDI/device registration, became mandatory on 28 May 2026, while the vigilance and PMS module remains under development.

contrary_evidence: Class I manufacturers prepare a PMS report rather than a PSUR, narrowing the initial PSUR customer segment.
EUDAMED's vigilance and PMS module is still under development, so near-term integration value is uncertain.
Established electronic quality-management and regulatory-information platforms already serve larger manufacturers.

economics.acquisition_route: A fixed-fee PMS traceability assessment, evidence-led technical content, direct outreach to small manufacturers, and QA/RA consultant referrals
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Modeled path: 150 customers at 36,000 PLN average annual recurring revenue equals 5.4m PLN ARR; a 40% owner-cash margin is 2.16m PLN/year and could produce more than 10m PLN over five mature years
economics.founder_time: Up to 5 hours/day for a two-customer design phase, with validation and regulatory review contracted to qualified specialists
economics.gross_margin_basis: Modeled 70-85% after secure hosting, validation maintenance, support, and contracted QA/RA review
economics.payback: Target under 9 months because onboarding is paid; regulated procurement and validation cycles are unmeasured
economics.pricing: Modeled 1,500-6,000 PLN/month by device-family and user count plus 15,000-50,000 PLN validated onboarding
economics.retention_or_repeat: PMS is continuous across the device lifetime and feeds recurring reports, risk updates, CAPA, and inspections

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A de-identified mapping corpus connecting event taxonomies, device exposure denominators, reviewer corrections, risk-file links, and accepted report structures
fingerprint.customer: EU medical-device manufacturers with a small regulatory team and roughly 1-20 Class IIa or IIb device families
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Technical PMS gap assessments, targeted outreach to small manufacturers, and referrals from independent QA/RA consultants
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Validated intake, deduplication, exposure-normalized trends, risk and CAPA linking, controlled drafting, review signatures, and report exports sold as regulated-workflow SaaS
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The manufacturer pays an annual license and onboarding fee when it needs continuous PMS control and a defensible PSUR or PMS report package
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A complaint, service event, literature review, trend calculation, CAPA, or periodic report cycle lacks a complete trace from raw evidence to approved safety conclusion

founder_fit: Health and data-analysis interests align with signal detection and evidence traceability, while the medical-student partner can improve domain vocabulary without acting as a regulator.
The founder can build a narrow analytics and workflow layer rather than capital-intensive hardware or a diagnostic medical device.
A small number of high-value customers can support meaningful revenue without mass consumer marketing or a public persona.
risks: A missed safety signal or incorrect trend could cause patient harm and severe liability.
Health, complaint, and device data create heightened security and privacy obligations.
Part-time founder availability may be incompatible with urgent customer incident expectations unless support is explicitly bounded.

structure.commercial_archetype: High-trust regulated evidence SaaS with paid validation and onboarding
structure.control_point: The audit trace from each post-market source event through signal analysis, benefit-risk decision, CAPA, approval, and periodic report statement
structure.critical_dependency: Manufacturers must provide complete source data and qualified regulatory personnel must approve every safety interpretation

thesis: Build a controlled evidence workbench for small EU Class IIa and IIb medical-device manufacturers that turns complaints, service events, literature findings, sales exposure, vigilance cases, and CAPA actions into traceable PMS analyses and review-ready PSUR sections. Manufacturers pay because continuous post-market surveillance crosses support, quality, clinical, distributor, and regulatory data, while every conclusion must link back to source evidence and approved risk decisions.
title: MDR Complaint-to-PSUR Evidence Workbench
uncertainties: The willingness of small manufacturers and notified bodies to accept AI-assisted drafting within a validated process is unknown.
The cost and duration of software validation, security review, and customer data migration may exceed the base budget.
Modeled pricing, acquisition cycle, specialist cost, support load, and owner-cash margin require paid validation.
